news.title: This National Team qualified for the World Cup. Now they are fundraising to get there.
news.lede: Men’s National Team, managed by the American Amputee Soccer Association, punched its ticket to the Amputee Soccer World Cup this fall. On top of work and training, the players have been fundraising to make sure they will be at the opening ceremony. This November, the United States will take on the best teams on the planet at the Amputee Football World Cup in San Juan de los Lagos, Mexico from Nov. The U.S. qualified on the field.

news.title: Bermuda close out Under-15 World Cup on a winning note
news.lede: Bermuda concluded their participation at the Fifa Under-15 World Cup & Festival in Baku, Azerbaijan, on a high with a 2-0 triumph over Jordan in a Tier D finals match today. Adam Barritt and co-captain De’Ari Trott scored for Aaron Denkins's side to end the tournament on a bright note. It was Bermuda’s third victory in the knockout and placement stage, following wins over Macao and Bahrain. From ten matches played in the whole tournament, Bermuda finished with five wins and the same number of defeats to place 117th of 189.

news.title: Junior Starlets reach U-17 World Cup knockouts for the first time
news.lede: Kenya’s U-17 women’s team thrashed Samoa 4-0 to reach the round of 16 at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup. This is only Kenya’s second appearance at the tournament. On their debut, in the Dominican Republic in 2024, they went out in the group stage. Japan are next for the Junior Starlets.

news.title: Players who defined an entire World Cup
news.lede: The World Cup has never felt like just another football competition. Every four years, it seems to produce players who step out of the ordinary and leave something lasting behind. It is not always the top scorer or even the captain of the winning side who stands out, but often the one who carries their team through the pressure and expectation. Some moments are defined by brilliance, others by controversy, yet certain players shape the entire feel of a tournament.

news.title: Fifa to miss equal Women’s World Cup prize money ambition set by Infantino
news.lede: Infantino said in 2023 equality was Fifa’s target. Prize money could double but big gap will remain. Fifa is to fall short of gender equality with the prize money on offer at next year’s Women’s World Cup, despite making a record $15bn (£11.2bn) in revenue from this summer’s men’s tournament. Gianni Infantino, the Fifa president, said in 2023 that the organisation’s ambition was to have equality for the prize pot for 2027, saying: “Fifa is stepping up with actions, not just with words.”
